extra.message: User input from request.GET['host'] is concatenated directly into an OS command passed to os.system() ("ping -c 1 " + host). An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g. host='127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd') resulting in remote command execution.

pickle.loads() is called on raw attacker-controlled data from request.body or the 'blob' GET parameter (optionally base64-decoded). Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary code execution on the server.

User input from request.GET['fragment'] is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This is server-side template injection: an attacker can supply template expressions (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__... }}) to read files or execute code, and the result is returned as text/html.

Attacker-controlled JSON from request.body is passed directly as a MongoDB find_one() filter (payload.get('filter', payload)). MongoDB operator injection (e.g. {"$gt": ""}) allows NoSQL injection to read arbitrary records from ops.records.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: lxml XMLParser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False and then parses raw request.body. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks: reading local files, SSRF, and denial of service via entity expansion.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The 'ref' GET parameter is interpolated directly into a filesystem path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") and written to via target.write_text(). A value like '../../tmp/pwned' escapes the export directory, allowing arbitrary file write. The file also contains attacker-supplied SSN and card values, compounding sensitive data handling issues.
The 'lane' parameter from GET/POST is passed unvalidated to redirect(). An attacker can supply an absolute external URL (e.g. lane=https://evil.com) causing an open redirect usable for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: course_grade_file_096 has no _wrk_gate check (unlike the neighboring handlers) and no @login_required; any unauthenticated remote user can call /ops/fold/course-grade-file-096/ and receive an ops memo referencing renewal risk, payment flags and owner contact details — sensitive data exposure without authentication.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Authorization in course_badge_gate_691 is based entirely on a client-controlled cookie ('ops_badge') or header ('x-ops-badge') equal to the literal string 'lead'. Any client can set badge=lead to obtain the 'elevated' lane exposing payroll and casework data — a trivial authentication/authorization bypass.

course_workset_rebind_208 applies workset.update(payload) with attacker-controlled JSON, allowing overwriting of security-relevant keys such as 'role', 'approved' and 'balance' (e.g. {"role": "admin", "approved": true}). This is a mass-assignment / parameter pollution flaw enabling privilege escalation semantics.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The request Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to 'true'. This allows any website to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses, defeating the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables TLS certificate verification for an outbound HTTPS request, exposing the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks.
course_frame_slip_671 explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy, deliberately disabling browser XSS and content-injection protections for the response.

course_identity_hint_651 uses a hardcoded verifier table known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"} embedded in source code as an authentication secret. Anyone with code access can bypass the verifier check.

response.set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) sets a cookie with attacker-influenced value and without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite attributes, leaving it accessible to JavaScript and transmissible over plaintext HTTP.

course_trace_panel_742 hardcodes trace_on = True and returns internal details (DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment value and the absolute BASE_EXPORT_DIR filesystem path) in a JSON response, disclosing internal configuration information useful to attackers.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The uploaded filename (drop_blob.name) and the 'packet_ref' GET parameter are passed directly to FileSystemStorage.save() as the storage path. Attacker-controlled filenames (relative paths) determine where content is written under the incoming export directory; Django only partially validates names, so crafted relative paths can clobber files in subdirectories.

SignUpForm exposes the 'role' field (with all ROLE_CHOICES including 'school_admin') on public self-registration, and signup() in core/views.py saves the form directly. Any anonymous visitor can register a school_admin (or instructor) account, gaining full administrative privileges — incorrect privilege assignment / privilege escalation.

export_grades verifies cohort membership only for instructors; a teaching assistant is authorized by the bare role check on line 785 without verifying they are assigned to this cohort (unlike api_cohort_students which checks both). Any TA can export the full gradebook (student names, points, feedback) for ANY cohort — broken access control / IDOR.

file_download performs no authorization check when resource.course is None (all files uploaded via file_upload have course unset) — any authenticated user can download any other user's uploaded file by guessing the pk. Additionally, teaching assistants fall through all checks even when a course is set. This is an IDOR / missing authorization flaw on user files.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: release_grade performs a state-changing action (marks grade released, notifies student) on a plain GET request with no @require_POST, so Django's CSRF middleware provides no protection. An instructor/admin can be tricked into releasing grades via a crafted link/image — cross-site request forgery.

assignment_status changes an assignment's lifecycle status (publish/close/archive) via a GET request with no POST requirement, making it CSRF-able — an attacker can cause an instructor to publish or archive assignments by tricking them into visiting a URL.

admin_user_toggle enables/disables arbitrary user accounts on a GET request with no POST requirement, allowing CSRF attacks that deactivate (or reactivate) user accounts when a school admin visits a malicious page.

request_resubmission mutates submission status and sends a notification on a GET request with no POST/CSRF enforcement, so an attacker can trigger resubmission requests on behalf of an instructor/TA via CSRF.
discussion_moderate changes thread status (pinned/locked/hidden) via a GET request with no POST requirement, exposing moderation actions to CSRF.
CSV user import assigns the hardcoded default password 'changeme123' when the CSV row lacks a password, creating accounts with a well-known credential that users are never forced to change.

get_client_ip trusts the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header unconditionally, and the value is persisted in AuditLog.ip_address. Attackers can spoof their IP in audit logs, undermining log integrity and any IP-based investigations.

cwe: CWE-348: Use of Less Trusted Source

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value 'django-insecure-local-dev-only' when the environment variable is unset. If deployed without the env var, Django session/CSRF signing keys are publicly known, enabling session forgery.
DATABASE_URL defaults to 'postgres://lms_user:lms_pass@localhost:5432/lms_db', embedding hardcoded database credentials in source code.

The seed command creates demo accounts (including 'admin_demo' with role school_admin) with hardcoded passwords such as 'AdminPass123!' and sets 'Password123!' for all seeded instructors/TAs/students. If run on a deployed instance these become well-known privileged credentials.
